title: Compactification data for the algebraization candidate
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring complete for an ideal $I$, let $f:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be separated and of finite type with $Z$ Noetherian, and set $Q=I\mathcal O_Z$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Let $G$ be a coherent formal $Q$-module whose first term has support proper over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base]. Let $q:Y\to Z$ be proper and let $e:Y\to\mathbf P^n_A$ be an immersion over $A$. Then there exist a Noetherian $P$, proper $p:P\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, an open immersion $j:Y\to P$ with $pj=fq$, and coherent modules $F'$ on $P$ and $F$ on $Y$ [pqf-def-coherent], such that $j^*F'\simeq F$, the $Q\mathcal O_Y$-adic completion of $F$ is isomorphic to $q^*G$, and $\operatorname{Supp}(F')\cap p^{-1}V(I)\subset j(Y)$. No support condition away from the closed fibre is asserted.

source.place: Theorem 088E, Chow compactification, projective algebraization, and boundary-support paragraphs

proof.text: Factor the supplied immersion through its scheme-theoretic image P, a closed subscheme of projective space, obtaining an open immersion j. Properness over the Noetherian A makes P Noetherian. Pull G back termwise; the formal pullback theorem gives coherence and quotient compatibility. Finite-type pullback support and the constant formal support lemma identify every term support with q inverse Supp(G_0), proper over A. Its image in the separated P is closed.

Extend the pulled terms by j_*. The coherent open pushforward lemma applies to their common closed support; all terms vanish off that support. Quotient compatibility on j(Y) and vanishing outside give a coherent formal system on P. Apply projective existence to obtain F prime. Restriction commutes with completion and yields F, the restriction isomorphism, and the desired completion isomorphism.

Nakayama at each point of the adic closed fibre identifies the support of F prime there with the support of its quotient by I. This quotient is the extended first term and is supported in j(Y). Thus the closed-fibre support containment holds. Boundary removal and proper-support transport are deliberately deferred to the proved support theorem.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 088E, proof paragraphs after Chow's lemma
